newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee drifts lower, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee drifts lower, seen rangebound.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures drifted lower in slow, post-holiday trade by midsession on Tuesday with values being pressured by light origin and trade selling.
Traders noted some commission house selling but this was not enough to prevent the slide.
Volume stood at a meagre 1,419 lots, dominated by July. Traders said business was expected to remain thin in view of lack of fresh fundamental inputs.

"Nobody wants to sell and there are no incentives to buy either," said one trader, noting that the market could continue to consolidate at current levels after last week's surge to the highest level since January 1996.
Benchmark July gapped $19 lower at the open and closed $13 down at $2,073 a tonne by the morning close. Its intraday high was $2,084.
Immediately, July is seen supported at $2,050. Traders said the current uptrend remained intact if July holds above $1,900.
On the upside, the main technical goal is $2,145, followed by the May 19 peak of $2,190, a level not seen since January 31, 1996.
The market was closed on Monday for a local holiday.
Generally, players are keeping a cautious stance in view of the current Brazilian cold season.
There was no damaging cold in Brazil's coffee belt over the weekend and no freeze was forecast for the rest of this week.
"But everybody wants to play safe now," another said.
The last severe frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, damaged some Brazil's coffee trees and sent world prices spiralling.
This morning, London's July/Sept was traded at $13-$14 while Sept/Nov $3-7.
In options, volume was small at 133 lots.
In other news, Japan's coffee stocks rose by a sharp 22.7 percent year on year to 67,298 tonnes in April as roasters rebuilt their low inventories following the steep price rally since January.
